Think twice about commissioning-heavy jobs if a weekend outage, several rounds of drawing redlines, or waiting for utility fault data will drain you. When a motor changes late, the single-line, load schedule and protection study all need another pass. If that rework feels like wasted time, look at a role with less responsibility for field changes before choosing plant power or commissioning.

Inputs

Send any equipment mismatch back to the design reviewer before releasing the schedule.

paragraphs: Section title | Work reality

A design day can mean marking up a feeder on a single-line, checking the breaker schedule, and writing why a drawing is on hold. At a utility or engineering consultancy, reviewers need traceable assumptions and a revision history. At a plant or controls integrator, the work may include a scheduled shutdown, a commissioning checklist and a handoff to maintenance.
Work settings | a utility design office, a controls integrator’s shop, or an electronics test lab. Site time depends on the assignment.
What you handle | load schedules, single-lines, breaker curves, I/O lists, circuit schematics and test traces.
Controls teams coordinate outage windows with operations. Product teams review prototypes before a design freeze.
Working hours | find out whether the team rotates night or weekend outages, or keeps the role on regular design hours.
Construction and maintenance need the same drawing revision and a clear list of checks to finish.
Review | compare drawing tags, equipment ratings and approved test conditions before releasing an update.

How to distinguish adjacent occupations

Electrical engineers turn equipment and system power requirements into a design, a verification plan, and an accountable handoff. Electricians typically install and maintain under the applicable authority, electronics engineers focus on circuits and signals, and technicians carry out approved checks and document exceptions.

Adjacent paths differ in responsibility levels (design approval versus installation, repair, and test support), objects (power and electrical systems versus electronics and hardware), and entry requirements (degrees, professional engineer licences, and employer authorization). Who does this occupation suit?
What education is required?
Are professional qualifications required?
Which track gives me the quickest feedback on my work?

A bench test can show a changed waveform in the same session. A distribution study may wait for equipment data and review. A controls change depends on the next outage or commissioning window. Pick the feedback rhythm you can work with.
Would I rather investigate a fault or settle a design trade-off?

In controls, trace the first alarm and see which interlock input changed. In design, compare two devices and explain the trade-off in current rating, space and lead time. Notice which kind of uncertainty you would rather resolve.
How should I assess income?
The May 2025 U.S. OEWS median for electrical engineers was $120,630 per year. Actual offers vary by region, industry and experience.
How do I compare an outage rotation with a design-office schedule?

Ask for the last scheduled outage window and see how this role hands off open tests. For a plant role, check who covers a late reset or a callout. For design work, ask which site visits you own and when drawing releases are due.
What skills are needed?

Electrical and power system fundamentals, standards and code systems, design calculation and simulation tools, drawing and documentation capabilities, and cross-disciplinary collaboration and written communication.

Complete an entire cycle through a paper design task: read requirements and standards, complete calculations and equipment selection, clearly state assumptions and margins, and provide conformity conclusions and limits.

Use the state examples here to identify the person who can seal your project documents.

values: Paper exercise inputs

Use the City of Poulsbo drawing in Sources. The 480 V three-phase schedule lists 144.68 kVA connected and 164.02 kVA calculated. The manual transfer switch (MTS) is marked 400 A and 100 kAIC. The notes list 20.1 kA maximum utility fault current. The motor control center (MCC) diagram says 400 V, while the schedule says 480 V.

Calculate current as kVA × 1,000 ÷ (√3 × 480). Compare calculated load with the 400 A marking, then compare the two fault figures on a separate line. Work from paper, with no equipment access or energization.
Keep drawing data, your calculations and the release decision on three separate lines.
What to submit
Hand in one annotated sheet with both load currents, the fault comparison, the voltage conflict, and the checks you would give the responsible reviewer.
Read the calculation and revision record together before accepting a field change.
Finish your own answer first

One point each: calculate both currents; compare the calculated load with 400 A; compare 20.1 kA with 100 kAIC; flag the 400/480 V conflict; document the hold and evidence needed.

paragraphs: At 480 V three-phase, 144.68 kVA is about 174 A and 164.02 kVA is about 197.3 A. The latter is below the marked 400 A. Keep the equipment check open: reconcile the drawing’s 400 V MCC label with the 480 V schedule, confirm the switch’s specified short-circuit rating and protective-device combination at 480 V, and verify fault duty at the equipment.

paragraphs: Entry, qualifications, and career development
Entry paths and evidence you can prepare
For internal product work, identify your design reviewer. For regulated public-project work, identify the PE in responsible charge before taking ownership of a release.

Texas (TBPELS) exempts qualifying work on a private employer’s own products or limited changes at facilities closed to the public. For Texas public works involving electrical engineering, the small-project exemption is for contemplated completed cost of $8,000 or less. Check other statutory exceptions and have the responsible Texas PE seal regulated work. California (BPELSG) exempts qualifying industrial electrical work tied to the corporation’s or affiliates’ products, systems or services. For regulated electrical work, including public projects, the California electrical engineer in responsible charge signs, seals and dates permitted or construction-release plans and specifications and final calculations and reports.

For U.S. licensure planning, ask the state board whether your degree and work supervision meet its rules before scheduling exams. An early-career design role can build the required record of experience, subject to the board’s rules.

A common U.S. route is a bachelor’s degree from an ABET-accredited engineering program, followed by the NCEES Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam and Engineer-in-Training (EIT) or Engineer Intern recognition where offered. For PE licensure, build documented, qualifying experience (typically four years) and pass the NCEES PE Electrical and Computer exam in the relevant discipline, such as Power. Some states allow the PE exam before the experience requirement is complete. The state board decides exam eligibility, accepted experience and when it can issue a license.

entries.answer: Follow a load from the equipment nameplate to the panel schedule, then record which device and protection settings support it. In controls the equivalent handoff is an interlock and test record. In power electronics it is a schematic and measured waveform.
entries.question: What do electrical engineers mainly do?

entries.answer: On a redesign, the electrical engineer rechecks the feeder and protection. The electronics engineer checks the board schematic and signals. An engineering technologist or technician may set up and run the tests, record results or update the drawing. The engineer assigned to release the design handles approvals and any seal required by law.
entries.question: How do electrical engineers, electronics engineers and engineering technologists differ?

entries.answer: Choose power if you want to review feeders and protective devices, controls if you want to debug I/O and interlocks, and power electronics if you want to trace component stresses and waveforms. Compare a single-line study, a commissioning test record and a circuit validation report before picking a course.
entries.question: Which electrical engineering track should I try first?

entries.answer: Start with guaranteed first-year cash. For example, a $110,000 base plus an $8,000 guaranteed payment totals $118,000. A $120,000 target that includes a $15,000 variable bonus guarantees $105,000 if the rest is base. Compare equity, overtime and callout pay separately. For leveling, ask who owns the fault study or field handoff and who signs. A real pay step has a higher written base or allowance for the expanded scope. If the job only updates panel tags or CAD drawings, ask what study you will get to check and when the level changes. Use local OEWS as a benchmark.

entries.answer: In 2026, use a model or an AI assistant to draft a test matrix, compare drawing revisions, or flag inconsistent tags. Check the source drawing and inputs yourself: a copied transformer impedance can change fault duty at every downstream bus. The engineer responsible for the design owns the assumptions, exception review and approval.

entries.answer: A utility or consulting team may send you to verify as-built equipment and ratings before issuing revised drawings. In a plant integration role, plan site time around the agreed shutdown and test window. In circuit development, the test bench and occasional supplier visits serve different purposes. Check the actual access and travel schedule in the posting.

subject.summary: A plant adds a motor, but the breaker shown on the old drawing no longer matches the panel schedule. An electrical engineer checks the load and fault duty, revises the single-line diagram, and records what can go forward and what needs review. The same discipline applies to controls and power electronics, with different tools and deliverables.
